name: real-retry-suppression
description: Write tests for retry suppression in reconcileFailedParents
system_prompt:
You are a coder agent implementing: Write tests for retry suppression in reconcileFailedParents

## Task

Add tests to reconcile_failed_parent_test.go verifying that reconcileFailedParents suppresses recovery when a parent task failed due to constraint-gate exhaustion and no new commits exist.

Test 1 (TestReconcileFailedParents_ConstraintGateExhausted_NoNewCommits): Create a bare repo with setupTestRepoWithMainBranch. Create a feature worktree using createFeatureWorktree. Get its HEAD SHA via worktree.RunGit(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], featureDir). Create a FAILED parent task with:
- WorktreeBranch: "feature/<name>"
- Context: {"constraint_gate_exhausted": true, "constraint_gate_failed_at_commit": "<HEAD SHA>"}
Create all subtasks as DONE. Call reconcileFailedParents(). Assert n=0 and parent remains FAILED.

Test 2 (TestReconcileFailedParents_ConstraintGateExhausted_NewCommit): Same setup, but after recording the SHA, add a new commit to the feature worktree using runGitCmd. The stored SHA should now differ from HEAD. Call reconcileFailedParents(). Assert n=1 and parent is recovered (status != FAILED). Also assert that `constraint_gate_exhausted` and `constraint_gate_failed_at_commit` are cleared from context after recovery.

Test 3 (TestReconcileFailedParents_NonConstraintFailure_StillRecovers): Create a FAILED parent with Context: {"failure_reason": "merge conflict"} (no constraint_gate_exhausted key). All subtasks DONE. Call reconcileFailedParents(). Assert n=1 — normal failures still recover.

Use setupReconcileTest (defined in reconcile_test.go) which returns (orch, db, bareRepo). Use createFeatureWorktree to make the feature branch. Use runGitCmd to add commits.

Import worktree package: `"github.com/godinj/drem-orchestrator/internal/worktree"` for RunGit calls.

The tests will initially fail because recoverFailedParent doesn't check exhaustion state yet.

## Working Directory

.

## Verification

Write all code changes, then run `go vet ./... && go test ./...` in a SINGLE bash command.
If tests fail, read ALL errors, fix in one pass, re-run once more. Max 2 verification cycles.

## Test Infrastructure Rules

- DB init in tests: use `testutil.NewTestDB(t)`, never `gorm.Open` directly.
- Shared test helpers live in `internal/testutil/testutil.go`; do not define local `createTest*`, `setupBareRepo`, etc.
- Use `testutil.SetupBareRepo(t)`, `testutil.CommitFile(t, ...)` for git test helpers.

## Commit

When tests pass, `git add` new/modified files and `git commit` with a descriptive message.
Do NOT push to remote.
